sections.title: 3. Introduction
sections.body:
### 3.1 Purpose
This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the business needs, scope, and functional/non-functional requirements for the 'refyne Chat' project, which is specified in the source document as a centralized Hospital Management System (HMS). The purpose is to provide a clear, unambiguous baseline for stakeholders, developers, and QA teams to ensure the system meets operational, clinical, and administrative needs.

### 3.2 Project Background
The source document outlines a need for a centralized platform to manage hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, and various clinical and administrative workflows. The system is designed to replace or consolidate disparate processes into a unified digital ecosystem supporting multiple user roles.

### 3.3 Business Problem
Currently, hospital operations may be fragmented across different systems or manual processes, leading to inefficiencies in patient management, appointment scheduling, billing, and clinical record-keeping. There is a need for a unified system that supports role-based access, real-time data visibility, and secure handling of sensitive medical information.

### 3.4 Business Objectives
| ID | Objective | Success Measure |
|----|-----------|-----------------|
| BO-01 | Centralize hospital operations | Single platform managing patients, appointments, billing, and inventory |
| BO-02 | Enhance patient experience | Patient portal for viewing appointments, prescriptions, and reports |
| BO-03 | Improve clinical efficiency | Integrated workflows for OPD/IPD, lab, pharmacy, and EMR |
| BO-04 | Ensure data security and compliance | Role-based access, encryption, and audit logs per HIPAA/GDPR |

### 3.5 Expected Business Benefits
- Reduced administrative overhead through automated workflows.
- Improved patient care via centralized electronic medical records (EMR).
- Enhanced operational visibility through dashboards and reporting.
- Compliance with healthcare data protection regulations (HIPAA, GDPR).
- Scalable architecture supporting future growth and integration.

sections.title: 4. Scope
sections.body:
### 4.1 In Scope
- Patient registration and profile management.
- Appointment scheduling and queue management.
- Doctor availability and scheduling.
- OPD/IPD management, including admission, discharge, and transfer.
- Electronic Medical Records (EMR) including diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
- Laboratory test requests and reports.
- Pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory.
- Bed/ward management.
- Billing, payments, insurance management, invoices, and receipts.
- Hospital expenses and staff management.
- Inventory and procurement.
- Patient portal for viewing appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history.
- Doctor dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
- System-wide features: dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role-based authorization.

### 4.2 Out of Scope
- Not explicitly defined in source documentation — pending stakeholder input.

### 4.3 System Boundaries
The system is a centralized platform with separate modules for Authentication, Patients, Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, Laboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration. It supports cloud or on-premise deployment and integrates with external systems for insurance, payments, and potentially lab/pharmacy vendors (specific integrations not detailed in source).

sections.title: 7. Business Process Overview
sections.body:
### 7.1 AS-IS Process
Not explicitly defined in source documentation — pending stakeholder input.

### 7.2 TO-BE Process
The TO-BE process involves centralized digital workflows:
1. **Outpatient (OPD) Workflow**: Patient registration → Appointment scheduling → Consultation → Diagnosis → Laboratory/Pharmacy → Billing → Follow-up.
2. **Inpatient (IPD) Workflow**: Admission → Bed allocation → Treatment → Investigations → Discharge → Final billing.

### 7.3 Process Flow Narrative Description
Patients are registered and assigned unique profiles. Appointments are scheduled based on doctor availability. During consultations, doctors record diagnoses, prescriptions, and clinical notes in the EMR. Laboratory and pharmacy modules process test requests and prescriptions, respectively. Billing is generated based on services rendered, and payments are processed. For inpatients, bed allocation is managed, and treatment progress is tracked until discharge, followed by final billing. All actions are logged for audit purposes, and patients can access their records via the portal.

sections.title: 9. Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### Module: Authentication
- **FR-001**: Implement secure authentication using JWT/OAuth.
  - **Description**: Users must log in with valid credentials.
  - **Preconditions**: User account exists.
  - **Input**: Username, password.
  - **Processing**: Validate credentials, generate JWT token.
  - **Output**: Authenticated session.
  - **Business Rules**: Passwords must be encrypted; sessions must expire after inactivity.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a valid user, When they enter correct credentials, Then they are granted access.

### Module: Patients
- **FR-002**: Manage patient registration and profiles.
  - **Description**: Create, update, and retrieve patient records.
  - **Preconditions**: None.
  - **Input**: Patient demographic and medical data.
  - **Processing**: Validate data, store in database.
  - **Output**: Unique patient ID and profile.
  - **Business Rules**: Patient ID must be unique; required fields must be filled.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a new patient, When registration is submitted, Then a unique profile is created.

### Module: Appointments
- **FR-003**: Schedule and manage appointments.
  - **Description**: Book, modify, and cancel appointments.
  - **Preconditions**: Patient and doctor exist.
  - **Input**: Appointment date, time, doctor ID.
  - **Processing**: Check availability, update schedule.
  - **Output**: Confirmed appointment.
  - **Business Rules**: Appointments cannot overlap for the same doctor.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given an available slot, When an appointment is booked, Then it is confirmed.

### Module: EMR
- **FR-004**: Maintain electronic medical records.
  - **Description**: Record diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
  - **Preconditions**: Patient exists.
  - **Input**: Clinical data.
  - **Processing**: Validate and store data.
  - **Output**: Updated EMR.
  - **Business Rules**: EMR entries must be timestamped and attributed to the user.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a patient, When clinical data is entered, Then it is saved to the EMR.

### Module: Laboratory
- **FR-005**: Process lab test requests and reports.
  - **Description**: Create lab requests, process tests, and generate reports.
  - **Preconditions**: Patient exists.
  - **Input**: Test type, patient ID.
  - **Processing**: Update status, generate report.
  - **Output**: Lab report.
  - **Business Rules**: Reports must be linked to the patient's EMR.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a lab request, When the test is completed, Then the report is available.

### Module: Pharmacy
- **FR-006**: Manage prescriptions and medicine inventory.
  - **Description**: Validate prescriptions, dispense medicines, and update inventory.
  - **Preconditions**: Prescription exists.
  - **Input**: Prescription ID, quantity.
  - **Processing**: Check inventory, update stock.
  - **Output**: Dispensed medicine record.
  - **Business Rules**: Inventory levels must be tracked; low stock alerts must be triggered.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a valid prescription, When medicine is dispensed, Then inventory is updated.

### Module: Billing
- **FR-007**: Generate bills and process payments.
  - **Description**: Create invoices, process payments, and manage insurance claims.
  - **Preconditions**: Services rendered.
  - **Input**: Service details, payment method.
  - **Processing**: Calculate total, update payment status.
  - **Output**: Invoice and receipt.
  - **Business Rules**: Payments must be reconciled with invoices.
  - **Given/When/Then**: Given a completed service, When a bill is generated, Then it is payable.

sections.title: 10. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### 10.1 Performance
- Fast API responses (target: < 2 seconds for standard queries).
- Scalable architecture to handle concurrent users.

### 10.2 Security
- PHI encryption at rest (AES-256) per HIPAA §164.312.
- Secure authentication (JWT/OAuth) and password encryption.
- HTTPS for all data transmission.
- Audit trail immutability per HIPAA §164.312(b).

### 10.3 Availability
- High availability with RTO < 1h and RPO < 5min per domain benchmarks.
- Regular backups and disaster recovery plans.

### 10.4 Scalability
- System must scale horizontally to support increased user load.
- Cloud or on-premise deployment options.

### 10.5 Usability
- Responsive web UI for all user roles.
- Intuitive dashboards and search/filtering capabilities.

### 10.6 Maintainability
- Modular architecture with separate components for each functional area.
- Comprehensive logging and error handling.

### 10.7 Compatibility
- Support for modern web browsers.
- Integration with external systems via REST APIs.

sections.title: 11. Business Rules
table: Each patient must have a unique identifier in the system.
All EMR entries must be attributed to the user who created them.
Pharmacy inventory must be updated in real-time upon dispensing.
All payments must be reconciled with corresponding invoices.
Users can only access modules and data permitted by their role.

sections.title: 12. Data Requirements
sections.body:
### 12.1 Data Entities List
- Patient
- Doctor
- Appointment
- EMR (Electronic Medical Record)
- Laboratory Test
- Prescription
- Medicine Inventory
- Bed/Ward
- Invoice
- Payment
- Staff

### 12.2 Data Fields
| Entity | Field | Data Type | Required | Description |
|--------|-------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Patient | Patient ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the patient |
| Patient | Name | String | Yes | Full name of the patient |
| Patient | Date of Birth | Date | Yes | Patient's date of birth |
| Appointment | Appointment ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the appointment |
| Appointment | Date | Date | Yes | Date of the appointment |
| EMR | Record ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the EMR entry |
| EMR | Diagnosis | String | No | Diagnosis recorded by the doctor |
| Prescription | Prescription ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the prescription |
| Prescription | Medicine | String | Yes | Name of the prescribed medicine |
| Invoice | Invoice ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the invoice |
| Invoice | Total Amount | Decimal | Yes | Total amount due |

### 12.3 Data Validation
- Required fields must be validated before saving.
- Data types must match defined schemas.
- Unique constraints must be enforced for IDs.

### 12.4 Data Retention
- Medical records must be retained per HIPAA and local regulations.
- Audit logs must be immutable and retained for a minimum of 6 years (per HIPAA).

sections.title: 14. Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### 14.1 User Interface
- Responsive web UI for all user roles.
- Dashboards for doctors, nurses, and administrators.
- Patient portal for self-service.
- Search and filtering capabilities across all modules.

### 14.2 API Interface
- REST APIs for all functional modules.
- JWT/OAuth-based authentication for API access.
- Standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

### 14.3 Hardware Interface
- Not explicitly defined in source documentation — pending stakeholder input.

sections.title: 18. Assumptions and Dependencies
sections.body:
### Assumptions
- Users have basic computer literacy.
- Internet connectivity is available for cloud deployment.
- External systems (insurance, payments) provide stable APIs.

### Dependencies
- Integration with external insurance and payment systems.
- Availability of HL7 FHIR standards for lab data exchange.
- Compliance with HIPAA and GDPR regulations.

sections.body:

- **Technology**: React/Next.js for frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, Redis for caching/queues.
- **Regulatory**: Must comply with HIPAA, GDPR, HL7 FHIR, and DICOM standards.

Implement AES-256 encryption, regular security audits
Use standardized APIs (HL7 FHIR, REST), conduct integration testing
Implement high availability, regular backups, disaster recovery plans

sections.title: 21. Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
The system will be accepted when:
1. All functional requirements (FR-001 to FR-007) are implemented and tested.
2. All non-functional requirements (performance, security, availability) are met.
3. User acceptance testing (UAT) is completed with no critical defects.
4. Compliance with HIPAA and GDPR is verified.
5. Documentation (user manuals, API docs) is complete and approved.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
